content.value_statement: Async Python code often fails due to blocking calls, unbounded tasks, and weak cleanup. This skill provides reusable asyncio patterns, examples, and references for robust concurrent services.
actual_capabilities: Provides asyncio examples for gather, semaphores, TaskGroup, timeouts, and async context managers.
Documents aiohttp client patterns, file transfer, WebSocket use, retries, and bounded requests.
Explains retry backoff, circuit breakers, partial failure handling, and structured result objects.
Shows production lifecycle patterns for shutdown, health checks, connection pools, and signal handling.
Includes a shell script that reports blocking calls in local Python files.
Includes an async project template with aiohttp session management and graceful cleanup.
limitations: It does not execute or validate generated code automatically.
Examples may need changes for specific Python versions, frameworks, and deployment rules.
The shell script requires ripgrep and scans local files only.
Network examples use demo URLs and should be replaced before production use.

use_cases.title: Refactor Blocking Coroutines
use_cases.description: Find blocking calls, missing awaits, and task management issues in async Python services.

use_cases.title: Design Concurrent HTTP Clients
use_cases.description: Plan aiohttp clients with bounded concurrency, retries, timeouts, and structured responses.

use_cases.title: Prepare Async Code For Production
use_cases.description: Add shutdown handling, health checks, resource cleanup, and safer failure behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Choose An Async Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner guidance for a new async task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the asyncio pattern I should use for this task: [describe task]. Include risks around blocking calls and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Review A Coroutine
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this async Python function for blocking calls, orphaned tasks, missing timeouts, and cancellation problems: [paste function].

prompt_templates.title: Design HTTP Concurrency
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for external API calls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an aiohttp client flow for these endpoints: [list]. Include bounded concurrency, retries, timeouts, and result handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Async Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for deployed async systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production async service architecture for [service]. Cover lifecycle management, health checks, shutdown, backpressure, and observability.

output_examples.input: Audit an async scraper that slows down under load.
output: Identifies unbounded concurrency as the likely cause.
Recommends semaphore limits, connection pooling, and per-request timeouts.
Lists tests for cancellation, retries, and partial failures.

output_examples.input: Design a background worker for API calls.
output: Proposes a queue based worker model with bounded throughput.
Adds retry backoff, shutdown handling, and tracked task cleanup.
Calls out metrics for failures, latency, and queue depth.

output_examples.input: Explain why a coroutine blocks the event loop.
output: Shows which operations are synchronous and why they block progress.
Suggests async libraries or executor isolation for those operations.
Highlights where timeouts and cancellation handling are missing.

best_practices: Set explicit timeouts on network and background operations.
Bound concurrency with semaphores, queues, or worker pools.
Track created tasks and shut them down during application cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not call blocking I/O directly inside coroutines.
Do not create fire-and-forget tasks without references.
Do not gather unlimited work without backpressure.

faq.question: What Python versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It recommends Python 3.10+. Some examples use Python 3.11 features, such as TaskGroup and timeout.

faq.question: Does it include runnable files?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an async project template and a shell script for finding blocking calls.

faq.question: Can it help with aiohttp?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers client sessions, retries, file transfer, WebSocket use, and bounded request patterns.

faq.question: Does it replace testing?
faq.answer: No. You still need unit, integration, cancellation, and load tests for your application.

faq.question: Can Claude or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill make network requests automatically?
faq.answer: No. Network calls appear in examples and templates that a user must run or adapt.
